problems.quote: 'tighten the repo rate' is a fixed phrase in policy discourse
problems.problem: Central banks do not 'tighten the repo rate'; they 'raise' or 'hike' the repo rate to tighten monetary policy. 'Tighten' collocates with 'monetary policy', not the rate itself.
problems.correction: 'raise the repo rate' is a fixed phrase in policy discourse
problems.verifierReason: 'Tighten' collocates with policy/stance, not the rate; 'raise the repo rate' is standard usage.

problems.quote: “approve” and “acknowledge” are positive polarity verbs that become infelicitous under negation
problems.problem: “Approve” and “acknowledge” are not positive polarity items; they are ordinary verbs fully compatible with negation (e.g., “did not approve” is natural). Positive polarity items (e.g., “some”, “already”) resist negation, but these verbs do not.
problems.correction: “approve” and “acknowledge” are ordinary verbs compatible with negation; they are not positive polarity items
problems.verifierReason: Original mislabels verbs as PPIs; they are fully negatable. Correction accurate.

problems.quote: Options like “proof” or “confirmation” are positive polarity and create a semantic clash
problems.problem: “Proof” and “confirmation” are not positive polarity items; they are ordinary nouns that freely occur in negative contexts (e.g., “no proof”, “no confirmation”). Positive polarity is a property of specific lexical items like “some”, not of nouns denoting evidence.
problems.correction: Options like “proof” or “confirmation” are ordinary nouns compatible with negation; they are not positive polarity items
problems.verifierReason: Original mislabels nouns as PPIs; they freely occur in negative contexts. Correction accurate.

problems.problem: “Yield” and “benefit” are not negative polarity items; the NPI in the example is “any”, which is licensed by the affective predicate “doubts”. The verbs/nouns themselves are not polarity-sensitive.
problems.correction: licensing the NPI “any”; “yield” and “benefit” are ordinary verbs/nouns, not NPIs
problems.verifierReason: Original misidentifies verbs/nouns as NPIs; NPI is 'any'. Correction accurate.

problems.quote: “provide” (will provide liquidity) changes the transitivity pattern and breaks the ellipsis licence
problems.problem: Both “cut” and “provide” are transitive verbs taking direct objects; “provide” does not change transitivity or break ellipsis. “The bank will cut rates and provide liquidity” is grammatical and parallel.
problems.correction: “provide” shares the same transitivity as “cut” and coordinates freely under the auxiliary “will”
problems.verifierReason: Original claims transitivity mismatch; both verbs transitive, coordination grammatical. Correction accurate.

problems.problem: Meronymy is a part-whole relation; 'governor' is not a part of 'member' but a type of member (hyponymy) or a role. The chain mislabels the semantic relation.
problems.correction: meronymy (part-of: committee → member) or hyponymy (type-of: member → governor)
problems.verifierReason: Original mislabels hyponymy as meronymy; correction correctly separates part-whole and type-of relations.
